title: “Monks, whatever is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being. And what, monks, is not yours? Form, monks, is…
content: “Monks, whatever is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being. And what, monks, is not yours? Form, monks, is not yours — abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being. Feeling … Perception … Formations … Consciousness is not yours — abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being.”

title: “Monks, what is clinging and worry? Here, monks, an untaught ordinary person, not seeing the noble ones, not skilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained…
content: “Monks, what is clinging and worry? Here, monks, an untaught ordinary person, not seeing the noble ones, not skilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained in the noble Dhamma, not seeing the true persons, not skilled in the true Dhamma, not trained in the true Dhamma, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. For him, that form changes and alters. Because of the change and alteration of form, his consciousness follows that change in form. Worrying states arise from that consciousness following the change in form, invading his mind and remaining. Because his mind is invaded, he is terrified, distressed, and full of longing and worry.”

title: Elder Mahā-Moggallāna: With hut whose roof is made of bones, Sewn together with sinews and flesh — Foul, full of stench! Carrying other people’s limbs…
content:
Elder Mahā-Moggallāna:

With hut whose roof is made of bones,
Sewn together with sinews and flesh —
Foul, full of stench!
Carrying other people’s limbs
As my own body!

The container full of feces,
Covered over with skin —
O female demon!
With your breasts like boils —
Your body has nine streams,
Always flowing.

Your body’s nine streams,
Foul, creating bondage —
The monk avoids that body
As a clean person avoids feces.

If others knew you
As I know you,
They would avoid you
As one avoids feces in the rain.

It is truly so, O Great Hero,
As the ascetic said:
Here, some are stuck,
Like an old ox in the mud.

One who thinks he can dye
The sky with turmeric,
Or with any other color —
That one only fails.

My mind is like that sky —
Well concentrated internally —
Do not bring evil thoughts to it,
Like a bird falling into a pile of fire.

title: One who does not lust for forms, Seeing a form, does not cling, His mind does not adhere to the feeling, He does not remain…
content:
One who does not lust for forms,
Seeing a form, does not cling,
His mind does not adhere to the feeling,
He does not remain attached to forms.
As he sees forms,
Feeling feelings accordingly,
It wanes away, not accumulated —
Thus mindful he practices.
Thus suffering is not stored up,
He is said to be close to Nibbāna.

One who does not lust for sounds,
Hearing a sound, does not cling …
One who does not lust for odors,
Smelling an odor, does not cling …
One who does not lust for tastes,
Tasting a flavor, does not cling …
One who does not lust for touches,
Feeling a touch, does not cling …

title: “What is the cause, good sirs, what is the condition for the non-arising of unarisen greed, or for the abandonment of arisen greed?” - “The…
content: “What is the cause, good sirs, what is the condition for the non-arising of unarisen greed, or for the abandonment of arisen greed?” - “The sign of the foul.” For one who attends wisely to the sign of the foul, unarisen greed does not arise and arisen greed is abandoned. This, good sirs, is the cause, this is the condition for the non-arising of unarisen greed and for the abandonment of arisen greed.

title: “Monks, I do not see any other class of things that is as diverse as the mind. Those beings in the animal realm — such…
content: “Monks, I do not see any other class of things that is as diverse as the mind. Those beings in the animal realm — such beings are diverse because of their minds. Therefore, monks, one should constantly reflect on one’s own mind thus: ‘For a long time, this mind has been defiled by greed, hatred, and delusion. Through the defilement of the mind, beings are defiled. Through the purification of the mind, beings are purified.’”

title: “Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—these are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing.…
content: “Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—these are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. Sounds cognizable by the ear … Odors cognizable by the nose … Tastes cognizable by the tongue … Tangibles cognizable by the body—these are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. These, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure.”

title: Though warned by the divine messengers, Young men remain heedless, They sorrow for a long time, Born in a low state. But the true person…
content:
Though warned by the divine messengers,
Young men remain heedless,
They sorrow for a long time,
Born in a low state.
But the true person here,
Warned by the divine messengers,
Is never heedless
In the noble Dhamma.
Seeing fear in clinging,
In birth and death,
Released from clinging,
Birth and death are ended.
Attaining security and bliss,
Here and now fully extinguished,
All enmity and fear —
They have overcome all.
All pain and sorrow —
All are transcended.

title: “‘Come, monk, guard the sense faculties. When you see a form with the eye, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular…
content: “‘Come, monk, guard the sense faculties. When you see a form with the eye, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the eye faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — restrain that cause, guard the eye, practice restraint of the eye. When you hear a sound with the ear … smell an odor with the nose … taste a flavor with the tongue … feel a touch with the body … cognize a phenomenon with the mind, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the mind faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — restrain that cause, guard the mind, practice restraint of the mind.’”

title: “Pleasant and delightful are sensual pleasures, In various forms both coarse and refined — Seeing the danger in these strands of pleasure, Wander alone like…
content:
“Pleasant and delightful are sensual pleasures,
In various forms both coarse and refined —
Seeing the danger in these strands of pleasure,
Wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.”

“This is a boil, this is a calamity,
This is a disease, this is a dart —
Seeing the danger in these strands of pleasure,
Wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.”
